title: The Discriminant
short: b² − 4ac tells how many real solutions there are.
trouble: Students think a negative discriminant means they made an arithmetic slip, when it means the parabola never meets the x-axis.

blocks.html: The expression under the square root in the quadratic formula, $b^2 - 4ac$, is called the discriminant. Before solving anything, it tells you how many real solutions to expect.

The formula is $x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{D}}{2a}$ with $D = b^2 - 4ac$. If $D > 0$, then $\pm\sqrt{D}$ gives two different numbers: two real solutions. If $D = 0$, then $\pm 0$ is just $0$: one solution, $x = -\frac{b}{2a}$. If $D < 0$, there is no real square root at all: no real solutions. On the graph these are a parabola crossing the $x$-axis twice, touching it at the vertex, or missing it entirely.

blocks.name: parabola
blocks.cap: Move $c$: the parabola crosses the $x$-axis twice, touches it once ($b^2 - 4ac = 0$), or floats above it with no real zeros.

blocks.html: $D = b^2 - 4ac$: positive means two real solutions, zero means one, negative means none.

blocks.title: Count the solutions
blocks.q: How many real solutions does $3x^2 - 2x + 4 = 0$ have?

blocks.title: Choose a value
blocks.q: For which $c$ does $x^2 + 8x + c = 0$ have exactly one solution?

blocks.title: Two irrational solutions
blocks.q: Without solving, describe the solutions of $x^2 - 2x - 1 = 0$.
steps: $8 > 0$, so there are two real solutions. Since $8$ is not a perfect square, $\sqrt{8}$ is irrational and so are the solutions ($1 \pm \sqrt{2}$).

blocks.html: A perfect-square discriminant ($0, 1, 4, 9, \ldots$) with whole-number $a$, $b$, $c$ means the solutions are rational, which is exactly when the quadratic factors nicely over the integers.

Thinking a negative discriminant means you made an arithmetic slip. It is a real result: the parabola never reaches the $x$-axis, so the equation has no real solutions. Check with the graph or a few values: $3x^2 - 2x + 4$ is positive for every $x$.
